messages:
aya: Heads-up — we saw a spike in preemptible evictions in us-west-2 around 07:12 UTC; tail latency for small-gen requests jumped ~2.3x. Any quick wins for blending instance types without blowing cost?

michael: Can you paste the eviction pattern / timestamped counts? Are these short bursts or sustained? :thinking:

aya: Short bursts, ~90s windows, ~15-30 nodes evicted in parallel (mostly p4d-ish types). Attached logs show node termination notices.

jonah: TLDR: mix compute-dense GPUs (high perf) with cheaper, lower-memory GPUs so short queues move to cheap nodes first. But packing policy matters — naive packing can increase preemptible collisions.

aya: thinking about a 2-tier preemptible pool: hot (low-latency) on high-perf but fewer nodes, cold (bulk) on cheaper cards. Anyone tried eviction-aware routing to cold first?

michael: We did something like that in staging last quarter. Routing rules: prefer cold for background batches & long-context jobs, prefer hot for short interactive requests. Key trick: keep cold nodes capped per AZ so a single AZ eviction doesn't drain both tiers.

jonah: Policy snippet we used (pseudo-yaml):
```yaml
pools:
  - name: hot
    instance_families: [p4d, a100-80g]
    max_pct: 25
    min_reserved: 5
  - name: cold
    instance_families: [a10g, t4, g4dn]
    max_pct: 60
    min_reserved: 20
routing:
  prefer_cold_for: [batch, rerank, embedding-indexing]
  prefer_hot_for: [interactive, chat, low-latency]
  az_spread_threshold: 0.2  # don't concentrate >20% of a pool in one AZ
```

sara: Two operational notes: 1) checkpoint frequency matters — for longer jobs increase checkpointing in cold nodes so eviction cost is low. 2) grace period handling: treat provider-termination-signal as soft-fail and spill to hot pool when possible.

aya: Can we quantify cost/perf for a mixed pool? I'm worried we lose efficiency if small requests move too often between families (added scheduling latency).

michael: Rough numbers from last run: hot (p4d) median latency 45ms, p50 cost unit 1.0. cold (a10g) median latency 120ms, p50 cost unit 0.35. If we route 70% traffic to cold we saved ~40% cost but tail latency increased ~1.8x. So tuning is workload dependent.

jonah: Also consider kernel-level perf variability across families — some ops (long KV cache) don't port well to smaller GPUs, causing weird CPU/GPU imbalance and queuing. Measure per-op tail latency before directing traffic.

aya: Good call. Ops: can infra run a 2-hr synthetic sweep tomorrow in us-west-2 with 3 mixes: (A) all-hot baseline, (B) 50/50 cold-hot, (C) cold-first routing config. Collect p50/p95/p99, evictions, and cost metrics.

infra-bot: Scheduled job #inc-789: gpu-mix-sweep will run 2026-03-19T07:00:00Z in us-west-2. Notified: @aya @michael @jonah @sara.

michael: Add these telemetry hooks to the sweep: per-route token latency, allocator queue length, node eviction time, and DGX-like kernel stalls (if available). Also log instance family per-request for attribution.

sara: Suggest adding a short-circuit: if eviction rate > X% in an AZ, switch to conservative mode: lock minimum hot capacity and route new sessions to other regions or hot nodes only. Helps preserve stability during provider storms.

aya: Agree. Propose X = 1.2% sustained over 3 min for AZ. Jonah, can you draft the conservative-mode switch threshold & rollout playbook?

jonah: On it. I'll draft an ops playbook: detection, automatic switch, alerting, rollback. Will include cost delta analysis so on-call can decide manual override. ETA end of day.

aya: Thanks. One more ask — can we estimate cold->hot spill cost when we requeue requests? I want worst-case monthly burn estimate for budget.

michael: I'll model that after the sweep and push numbers into the infra-cost dashboard. Expect a small spike but should be within reserved buffer if we cap hot spill to 10% of traffic.

sara: :thumbsup: Also make sure RBAC is set so only infra rotation can flip the conservative mode.

aya: Perfect. Closing the loop: sweep scheduled, playbook being written, telemetry hooks + conservative thresholds. Will post results in this thread. Thanks all.
